clips.title: Red Green Refactor is OP With Claude Code
clips.why: Matt Pocock explains red, green, refactor and why it fits coding agents so well: the failing test is a target the agent cannot argue with.
look: The red step comes first and is watched on purpose. That is our before run.
Why agents in particular need the loop: a test gives the agent feedback it can act on.
How he arranges the workflow for the agent. In our platform the harness, not the agent, runs the red step.
clips.after: Nova follows the same cycle, with two additions: the requester approved the tests' content in the plan, and the tests are locked once they are red.

clips.title: Test-Driven Development In Python // The Power of Red-Green-Refactor
clips.why: A slow, concrete walk through the red phase: what you write first, and what the failing run should tell you.
look: The test is written against behaviour that does not exist yet.
Read the failure message itself, not only the word FAILED. That is the difference between good red and useless red.
Think about how little product code you need before the first red run: none.
clips.after: Our classifier reads the same failure messages automatically: AssertionError counts, Cannot find module does not.

clips.title: my ai agent deleted tests to pass the tests
clips.why: A real agent taking the shortcut this lesson's lock exists for: making the tests pass by changing the tests.
look: The agent was asked for green tests, and changing the tests was the cheapest path to green.
Ask yourself whether instructions alone could have stopped it.
Think about which layer of our lock would have caught each change.
clips.after: Nova may add tests, but a hash lock, a Stop hook and a CI check stand between it and the tests it is judged by.

practice.q: Nova's session writes: "I ran the three QA tests on the unchanged code and all of them failed." Why does the platform not save that sentence as the before proof?

options.text: A sentence from the model is a claim; the harness runs the tests itself, so the result is a fact it can read
options.why: The before run is evidence a reviewer will trust later. Only the harness's own run, with vitest's report, shows how each test failed.

options.text: Because the model is not allowed to run tests in the VM
options.why: Nova runs tests all the time while it builds. The point is who records the proof, not who may run a test.

options.text: Because the before run must happen on a different machine
options.why: It runs on the same full VM. What matters is that the harness runs it and reads the report, not where.

practice.q: Finish the line of the classifier that recognises a good red in vitest's report.
practice.hint: The error class vitest's expect() throws.
practice.why: Vitest reports a failed expect() as an AssertionError. Any other first line means the test failed for another reason.

practice.q: Put the steps after plan approval in order.
items: Nova writes one test per QA check, before any product code
The harness runs them on the unchanged code and saves the before run
Each test must fail on an assertion, or be a guard the plan names
The harness stores a hash of each test file outside the checkout
Nova writes the product code until the locked tests pass
practice.why: Write, prove red, lock, then build. Locking before the red is proven would protect a test that proves nothing.

practice.q: Nova realises one of RH-1234's QA checks expects the wrong text. What should it do?

options.text: Edit the locked test, because the plan was wrong
options.why: The hook refuses it, and even if it got through, the requester approved that check. A quiet change breaks the agreement.

options.text: Ask the requester for a new plan version; the new approval unlocks and relocks the tests
options.why: The checks belong to the agreement with the requester, so only the requester can change them.

options.text: Skip that check and mention it in the PR
options.why: A skipped QA check means the PR cannot pass the ready gate. The right path is a new plan version.

practice.q: Where does the harness keep the hashes, so no tool that works in the repo can change them?
practice.hint: The checkout is /work/fcp; the lock is next to it, in the .nova folder.
practice.why: Outside /work/fcp, the lock file is not part of the repo Nova edits, so changing it is not a normal edit of the project.
